title.narrative: SPVO – Supporting smallholder farmers' livelihoods in the specialty coffee value chain

description.narrative: This project, led by This Side Up Coffee (TSU) and Abakundakawa Rushashi Cooperative, aims to address persistent inequality and poverty in the coffee value chain in northern Rwanda. While Abakundakawa produces specialty coffee of high quality, the limited production and small landholdings hinder the ability to lift coffee farmers out of poverty, which often results in inability of families to support school fees and is the main driver behind the prevalence of child labour. Moreover, the inaccessibility of healthcare as well as developing local infrastructure that can support women and young mothers care for their children is very weak or almost nonexistent. . Building Infrastructure for Women, Youth & ChildrenThe project supports the creation of community childcare facility, alongside dedicated on-farm shade and rest areas. This safe environment for children frees up women’s time, improves working conditions, and boosts farm productivity. Additionally, the project distributes personal protective gear and first-aid kits to mitigate health and safety risks. For local youth, setting up a modern ICT room delivers essential digital skills.Scaling Regenerative Farming and Soil ResilienceTo counter small landholdings and sub-optimal soil health, the initiative scales sustainable agricultural practices through hands-on restoration and income diversification. A 3-hectare, women-managed agroforestry plot serves as a model site, backed by the mass distribution of shade trees, fruit trees, cover crops, and mulch. Integrating a cooperative livestock scheme creates an organic fertilizer pipeline while opening new revenue streams for farming families. Comprehensive training reinforces these assets, equipping farmers with expertise in soil improvement, composting, fertilizer production, and organic pesticides. Strengthening Women's Empowerment, Access to Markets and TraceabilityBeyond the farm level, the project plan drives market access and economic self-sufficiency. Cooperative marketing and international trade show participation improve direct market access, complemented by coffee cupping and quality control education. The project explores alternative income generation pathways fow women (e.g. through a sewing project), vocational training, financial literacy programs, and savings group support. Transitioning to fully digital traceability systems and updating public communication platforms ensures fully transparency.
